title: Caring for someone on hospice
notes:
Comfort comes first. Hospice is in charge of the medical care, and we support the plan they set.

Call the hospice nurse first, not 911, for pain, trouble breathing, a fall, new skin problems, or anything that worries you, unless the hospice plan or the family tells you otherwise. Then call our office at (417) 234-8494.

The hospice phone number is in the folder in the home. Find it at the start of every shift.

title: Turning and repositioning
notes:
Turn every 2 hours, or as the care plan says. Rotate: left side, back, right side.

Use the draw sheet to move them. Never drag skin across the sheet.
Put a pillow between the knees and one behind the back when on the side.
Float the heels: a pillow under the calves so the heels do not touch the bed.
At every turn, look at the tailbone, hips, heels, elbows and ears.
Do not rub or massage red skin over a bone.

title: Skin checks and bed sores
notes:
The first sign of a bed sore is a pink or red spot over a bone that does not fade after the pressure is off.

Keep the skin clean and dry, especially after a bowel movement.
Take pressure off a red spot by turning them off it.
Tell the hospice nurse and our office the same day about a red spot that stays red, a blister, open skin, or a dark or purple area.

title: Bedside commode
notes:
Put the commode right next to the bed with its brakes or feet locked.
Use a gait belt for every transfer.
They must be able to stand and bear some of their own weight. If they cannot, do not lift them: keep them in bed, use a brief, and call our office.
Wear gloves. Empty and rinse the bucket after every use.

title: Changing a brief in bed
notes:
Roll them toward you, onto their side, and back, using the draw sheet.
Clean front to back, then dry the skin fully.
Check the skin while they are on their side.
Put a clean pad or sheet under them if the bed got wet or soiled.

title: PureWick for men (male external catheter)
notes:
From BD, the maker:

Putting it on: trim the hair, wash the skin with soap and water, rinse, and dry it completely. No creams, lotions or powder on that area, or it will not stick.
Check it and the skin at least every 2 hours, and after every turn: still connected, no pulling on the tube, no leaking.
Replace it at least every 24 hours, and right away if it gets stool or blood on it.
Taking it off: peel slowly from the top down, never pull straight off. A warm, damp cloth helps loosen it.
Empty the canister before it reaches 1800 mL. It holds 2000.
Tell the hospice nurse and our office about redness, sores or swelling.
